text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Thursday:
- International news: Front page leads with death of Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping.

- Europe: The European Union Parliament has threatened to call for a no-confidence vote in the European Commission by year-end if the Commission does not put into practice recommendations on mad cow disease.
- Switzerland: Federal Budget showed a deficit of 4.4 billion francs in 1996, which was about 400 million higher than expected. Revenues were 447 milllion below projections.

- The transport commission of the Swiss parliament wants to separate financing of large rail projects, including the NEAT tunnel, from other building projects. Financing would be done per special fund drawing from levies imposed on heavy vehicles.
- Econ/Business: Three Swiss banks gained dominance in leading new bond issues for Japanese borrowers in 1996.

- Econ/Business: The Economist Intelligence Unit has published a study showing over a third of the world's private investment is managed from Switzerland. The study of over 150 "tax havens" worldwide found that over 1.28 trillion francs was managed in Switzerland for private foreign investors.
- Business page leads on article about recent rally on Swiss bourse, questioning how much of latest gains are speculative. It notes that daily bourse volume has doubled or tripled.
- Editorials, front page lead on Deng.
